    private
    def validate_native_bindings!
      m,s,native = @manifest,@selection,@native_manifest
      Files.need(s.is_a?(Hash) && s["schema"] == SELECTION_SCHEMA &&
        s["sourceFormat"] == "SF100_SCAN" && s["datasetId"] == m["datasetId"] &&
        s["sourceKey"] == m["sourceKey"] && s["nativeManifestSha256"] == source_sha256 &&
        s["room"].is_a?(String) && File.expand_path(s["room"]) == s["room"] &&
        descriptor("selection.json")["sha256"] == m["selectionSha256"] &&
        descriptor("source.json")["sha256"] == m["sourceRecordSha256"] &&
        descriptor("native-receiving.json")["sha256"] == m["nativeReceiptSha256"],
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SELECTION_CHANGED")
      outputs,archives = self.class.check_receipt(@native_receipt,
        room: s["room"],manifest_sha256: source_sha256)
      Files.need(@files.keys.sort == (outputs+archives+METADATA).sort &&
        @native_receipt["sourceBindingSha256"] == m["sourceBindingSha256"],
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_COMPLETE_FILES_REQUIRED")
      (outputs+archives).each do |name|
        original = @native_delivery["outputs"][name] || @native_delivery["archives"][name]
        Files.need(%w[bytes sha256].all? { |key| original[key] == descriptor(name)[key] },
          "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ORIGINAL_FILE_CHANGED")
      end
      scan = @native_delivery.fetch("originalNativeScan")
      dataset = native.is_a?(Hash) && native["dataset"]
      Files.need(native.is_a?(Hash) && native["schema"] == "stellar-forge.buyer-delivery-manifest.v1" &&
        dataset.is_a?(Hash) && dataset["name"] == scan["name"] &&
        dataset["rows"] == row_count && row_count == scan["count"] &&
        dataset["snapshot"] == snapshot && snapshot == scan["snapshot"] &&
        dataset["projectedFields"] == fields && fields == scan["fields"] &&
        dataset["filters"] == scan["filters"] && dataset["ranges"] == scan["ranges"] &&
        dataset["order"] == (scan["order"] || "csv-record-order") &&
        dataset["originalQueryHash"] == scan["queryHash"] && HASH.match?(dataset["originalQueryHash"].to_s) &&
        dataset["originalQuerySignature"] == scan["pages"][0]["signature"] &&
        native["chainDigest"] == scan["chain"] &&
        native["paymentStatus"] == @native_delivery["paymentStatus"] &&
        native["sourcePages"].is_a?(Array) && native["sourcePages"].length == scan["pages"].length &&
        descriptor("manifest.json")["sha256"] == source_sha256 &&
        native["outputs"].is_a?(Hash) && native["outputs"].keys.sort == (outputs-["manifest.json"]).sort,
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ORIGINAL_MANIFEST_CHANGED")
      native["outputs"].each do |name,item|
        Files.need(item == descriptor(name).slice("bytes","sha256"), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ORIGINAL_OUTPUT_CHANGED")
      end
      original_session = json_file("session.json",limit: 4096)
      Files.need(original_session == scan["session"] &&
        original_session["schema"] == "stellar-forge.buyer-delivery.v1",
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SESSION_CHANGED")
      if @semantics
        binding = native["semantics"]
        Files.need(binding.is_a?(Hash) && binding == @native_delivery["semantics"] &&
          binding["file"] == "semantics.json" && binding["selectedFields"] == fields &&
          binding["scope"] == "PUBLISHED_DATASET" && binding["typedRowsFile"] == "dataset.jsonl" &&
          %w[schema sha256 definitionSha256].all? { |key| binding[key] == @semantics[key] } &&
          binding["captureManifestSha256"] == @semantics.dig("source","captureManifestSha256") &&
          @semantics == scan["semanticDocument"], "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SEMANTICS_CHANGED")
      else
        Files.need(native["semantics"].nil? && @native_delivery["semantics"].nil? &&
          scan["semanticDocument"].nil?, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SEMANTICS_CHANGED")
      end
      Files.need(@source.is_a?(Hash) && @source["schema"] == SOURCE_SCHEMA &&
        @source["sourceFormat"] == "SF100_SCAN" && @source["sourceKey"] == m["sourceKey"] &&
        @source["datasetId"] == m["datasetId"] && @source["originalRoom"] == s["room"] &&
        @source["sourceId"] == source_sha256 && @source["manifestSha256"] == source_sha256 &&
        @source["sourceBindingSha256"] == m["sourceBindingSha256"] &&
        @source["datasetName"] == dataset["name"] && @source["columns"] == @native_receipt["columns"] &&
        @source["providerIdentity"] == self.class.provider_identity(@semantics) &&
        @source["semanticsFile"] == (@semantics ? descriptor("semantics.json") : nil),
        "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_SOURCE_BINDING_CHANGED")
    end

    def same_typed_value?(left, right)
      return false unless left.class == right.class
      if left.is_a?(Hash)
        left.keys.sort == right.keys.sort && left.all? { |key,value| same_typed_value?(value,right[key]) }
      elsif left.is_a?(Array)
        left.length == right.length && left.zip(right).all? { |a,b| same_typed_value?(a,b) }
      else
        left == right
      end
    end

    # Reopening binds each original page record to its complete native JSONL.
    # Hash the native compact record bytes, preserving original number lexemes.
    def validate_original_rows!
      scan = @native_delivery.fetch("originalNativeScan")
      count,previous,cursor = 0,nil,nil
      intents,source_hashes = {},{}
      with_snapshot("dataset.jsonl") do |rows|
        scan["pages"].each_with_index do |page,index|
          Files.need(page.is_a?(Hash) && page["index"] == index && page["previous"] == previous &&
            page["requestCursor"] == cursor && page["returned"].is_a?(Integer) && page["returned"] >= 0 &&
            %w[chain sourceSha256 signature].all? { |key| HASH.match?(page[key].to_s) } &&
            INTENT.match?(page["intent"].to_s) && !intents[page["intent"]] && !source_hashes[page["sourceSha256"]],
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_PAGE_CHANGED")
          Files.need(page["signature"] == scan["pages"][0]["signature"], "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_QUERY_CHANGED")
          expected = {"index"=>index,"intent"=>page["intent"],"sourceSha256"=>page["sourceSha256"],
            "evidenceSha256"=>page["evidenceSha256"],"recordDigest"=>page["chain"],
            "rows"=>page["returned"],"requestedCursor"=>page["requestCursor"]}
          Files.need(@native_manifest["sourcePages"][index] == expected, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_PAGE_CHANGED")
          raw = file_bytes(format("pages/%05d.json",index),limit: MAX_PAGE)
          archive = Files.parse(raw,decimals: true)
          suffix = ',"chain":"' + page["chain"] + "\"}\n"
          Files.need(raw.end_with?(suffix) &&
            Files.hash(raw.byteslice(0,raw.bytesize-suffix.bytesize) + "}") == page["chain"] &&
            archive.is_a?(Hash) && archive["schema"] == "stellar-forge.buyer-page-archive.v1" &&
            %w[schema index previous intent requestCursor sourceSha256 evidenceSha256 signature chain].all? {
              |key| archive[key] == page[key]
            }, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ARCHIVE_CHANGED")
          payload = archive["payload"]
          Files.need(payload.is_a?(Hash) && payload["schema"] == "stellar-forge.dataset-page.v1" &&
            payload["fields"] == fields && payload.dig("dataset","snapshot") == snapshot &&
            payload.dig("dataset","name") == scan["name"] && payload["rows"].is_a?(Array) &&
            payload["rows"].length == page["returned"] &&
            payload.dig("page","returned") == page["returned"] && payload.dig("page","total") == row_count,
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_ARCHIVE_ROWS_CHANGED")
          columns = payload.dig("dataset","columns")
          Files.need(columns.is_a?(Array) && columns.all? { |column| column.is_a?(Hash) } &&
            fields.map { |name| columns.find { |column| column["name"] == name } } == @native_receipt["columns"] &&
            payload["semantics"] == @semantics, "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_PAGE_MEANING_CHANGED")
          payload["rows"].each do |original|
            line = rows.gets("\n",2_097_153)
            Files.need(line && line.end_with?("\n") && line.bytesize <= 2_097_152 &&
              same_typed_value?(Files.parse(line,decimals: true),original),
              "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_JSONL_SOURCE_CHANGED")
            count += 1
          end
          cursor = payload.dig("page","nextCursor")
          Files.need(count <= row_count && (index == scan["pages"].length-1 ? cursor.nil? : cursor.is_a?(String)),
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_PAGE_RANGE_CHANGED")
          if cursor
            Files.need(/\A[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,512}\z/.match?(cursor), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_CURSOR_CHANGED")
            decoded = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(cursor)
            Files.need(Base64.urlsafe_encode64(decoded,padding: false) == cursor &&
              Files.parse(decoded) == {"v"=>1,"s"=>snapshot,"q"=>scan["queryHash"],"n"=>count},
              "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_CURSOR_CHANGED")
          end
          previous = page["chain"]
          intents[page["intent"]] = true
          source_hashes[page["sourceSha256"]] = true
        end
        Files.need(rows.read(1).nil? && count == row_count && cursor.nil? && previous == scan["chain"],
          "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_COMPLETE_ROWS_REQUIRED")
      end
    end
  end
end

@contextmanager
def published_connection(filename, url):
    """Atomically publish one private connection, without replacing an existing file."""
    if filename is None:
        yield None
        return
    destination = Path(filename).expanduser().absolute()
    encoded = (url + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    descriptor, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="." + destination.name + "-", dir=destination.parent)
    temporary = Path(temporary)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as output:
            os.chmod(temporary, 0o600)
            output.write(encoded)
            output.flush()
            os.fsync(output.fileno())
        try:
            os.link(temporary, destination, follow_symlinks=False)
        except FileExistsError as error:
            raise InputError("Connection file already exists; use its running console, or remove a stale file after its process stops") from error
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    try:
        yield str(destination)
    finally:
        try:
            info = destination.lstat()
            if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and info.st_size == len(encoded) and destination.read_bytes() == encoded:
                destination.unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass

                signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN)
                try:
                    server.server_close()
                finally:
                    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, previous)
            return
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False))

# Merchant incident operations

Run the original SF93 collector continuously, retain an actionable incident, notify the configured operator, acknowledge it from another terminal, and bring its original baseline and recovery captures into the existing SF74 case desk. The watcher owns its process and private state. Existing seller, operations and SF98 delivery processes retain their own lifecycle.

## Watch an original Object buyer

The same watcher accepts a reviewed saved ObjectSession alongside existing seller
registrations. Use `review-object` to bind its exact session file, configuration and
original intent, then apply that selection through the existing configuration
revision. The watcher reads original per-request finalization views and verifies
saved output without purchasing, assembling or finalizing anything.

The [complete Object monitoring guide](OBJECT_MONITORING.md) covers bounded source
review, the five incident conditions, original notification handling and the full
SF74 case export/reopen flow. A missing view is not a zero payment or a completed
delivery; financial state, verified output and process observations remain
separate.

## Register and start

Requirements are Node 22 or newer, Linux with util-linux `flock`, the original SF30 seller plus its operations listener, and a private directory on a local filesystem supporting file locks, atomic rename and fsync. Run the watcher as the same operating-system user as its private files. A foreground invocation can also be supervised by the deployment's existing process manager; configure it to send SIGTERM and allow current bounded requests/state writes to finish.

Start the original seller and operations launcher as usual. Its printed seller and operations ports are the registrations used below. For example, the original source example uses seller port 8423 and operations port 8424:

```bash
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/operations/launch.mjs -- \
  --config stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/examples/service.json --port 8423
```

From another terminal, prepare a private configuration. Edit merchant IDs/labels and the exact original local ports. Up to eight merchants can share one watcher.

```bash
umask 077
mkdir -p /srv/stellar/operator
cp stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/examples/watch.json \
  /srv/stellar/operator/watch.json
chmod 600 /srv/stellar/operator/watch.json

SF93=stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" init \
  --config /srv/stellar/operator/watch.json --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" run --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents
```

`init` creates a new private state directory and never overwrites one. Its parent must exist. `run` reopens that same directory. One watcher holds the original parent-owned kernel lease; a second watcher cannot start against the same state. SIGINT/SIGTERM cancels its pending HTTP reads, finishes its state write and releases its own lease. A crash releases the kernel lock without a PID-file override. The `lease.lock` files are permanent lock inodes: do not remove them.

Provide `SF93_NOTIFICATION_URL` and `SF93_NOTIFICATION_SECRET` through the process environment or existing secret manager. The signing secret must contain at least 32 UTF-8 bytes. Configuration/state retain environment variable names and the canonical endpoint's digest, never the resolved URL or signing secret. Set `notification: null` to use local incident operation without a hook. Missing or invalid hook configuration records a paused notification while local collection and incident work continue. The default endpoint must use HTTPS. Explicit `allowLoopback: true` additionally permits an HTTP receiver on `127.0.0.1:PORT` for local integration.

The original seller health, offers, operations snapshot and metrics are read through four fixed GET paths, with a two-million-byte response bound and a five-second absolute deadline per read. When a merchant has a `delivery` policy, the watcher also reads the original private `/api/delivery` projection. It never calls a merchant resource to check whether a purchase succeeds.

## Conditions and recovery

| Condition | Original observation | Clear condition |
|---|---|---|
| `ENDPOINT_UNAVAILABLE` | Failed required endpoint read, invalid original packet or same-session counter/clock discontinuity | A complete valid four-endpoint capture |
| `OBSERVER_INCOMPLETE` | Detached observer or nonzero original `observerErrors` | An attached native observer with zero errors |
| `HTTP_5XX` | Configured minimum and percentage of 5xx among responses in original minute buckets | A complete clean source window below the configured threshold |
| `DISCONNECTED` | Configured minimum and percentage of disconnected attempts among completions | A complete clean source window below the configured threshold |
| `DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE` | Required original outbox projection unavailable or invalid | A valid available original projection |
| `DELIVERY_BACKLOG` | Original pending work has reached its configured oldest age | A valid projection with no qualifying old pending work |
| `DELIVERY_EXHAUSTED` | Original exhausted deliveries reach the configured count | A valid projection below that count |

`failurePolls` and `recoveryPolls` count consecutive usable observations. Unknown observations break a streak; an unavailable source cannot close its traffic/delivery incidents. Acknowledgment records human ownership but does not change whether the source is failing. A condition can open again as a new incident after a measured recovery.

`windowMinutes` selects the original collector's current minute bucket and preceding buckets. It preserves the original event clocks: completion counts can include requests started earlier. Counts are read directly from those buckets; this product maintains no parallel traffic collector. An observed positive failure can open an incident in a partial session. Clearing a traffic incident requires the observer to have been attached since the selected window began, with no observer errors. On a new session UUID, the watcher resets consecutive coverage state and retains existing incidents. It never subtracts the new counters from the old session. Same-session cumulative counters must not go backwards.

The original `observerErrors` count is cumulative. Any nonzero value keeps `OBSERVER_INCOMPLETE` active for that native session and prevents a traffic incident from claiming complete recovery. Restore a clean original observer/session, then allow its real window to fill. Waiting for an old error to age out of the request buckets does not clear the cumulative observer condition.

The attached original SF98 journal projection supplies the actual backlog counters and capture time. `delivery.required: false` permits a merchant without an attached outbox; a missing projection still cannot resolve an existing delivery incident. Set `delivery: null` to omit that merchant's delivery monitoring entirely. Payment challenges are normal 402 responses and do not trigger an incident. HTTP responses, notification acceptance and original delivery counters are distinct from independent on-chain payment confirmation.

## Acknowledge and follow through

Read actual IDs and revisions from the private status output:

```bash
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" status --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" ack --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents \
  --incident ACTUAL_INCIDENT_UUID --revision 1 --by 'Merchant operator' \
  --note-file /srv/stellar/operator/repair-note.txt
```

The optional note file must be private and at most 2,000 bytes. Notes stay in private state/support handoffs. They are never put into hook payloads. The acknowledgment command holds a short original kernel transaction lease, so it works while the watcher is collecting. Its incident revision prevents accidentally acknowledging a different state after a concurrent recovery. The frequently changing overall directory revision is not the operator's concurrency token.

`status --details` includes retained incident signals and notes. The worker fields describe its last recorded process, start, sweep and stop times. A stale `RUNNING` record after a crash is a historical heartbeat, not evidence that its PID still owns a live process. Ownership comes from the kernel lease. If no recent sweep appears, inspect the actual watcher process/service before relying on alert freshness.

After repairing/restarting the original seller or delivery worker, leave the watcher running. Successful native observations close the incident as `RECOVERED`, attach the original follow-up capture and enqueue a recovery notification. The initial session, latest failing session and recovery session remain separate fields. Original traffic completeness rules continue to apply across a restart.

## Notification delivery and destination changes

For a Slack channel, use the original queue's `transport: "slack"` configuration
and [Slack operating guide](SLACK_OPERATIONS.md). It verifies the selected
workspace, posts transitions into the same retained incident thread, saves
Slack channel/timestamp receipts and preserves provider rate waits through
restart. The `destination` command checks the configured actor/workspace.
The webhook configuration below retains its original body and signature format.

Payload schema is `stellar-forge.seller-incident-notification.v1`. It contains stable event/incident IDs, the registered merchant ID, condition, transition, current incident status, timestamps, source session and explicitly selected numeric counts. It contains no merchant endpoint, full offer, amount/payee, URL/query/header/body, acknowledgment note or raw network error.

The receiver validates these headers against the exact received UTF-8 body:

```text
x-starforge-event-id: EVENT_UUID
x-starforge-timestamp: UNIX_SECONDS
x-starforge-signature: sha256=HEX_HMAC_SHA256
```

The HMAC input is `timestamp + "." + exactBody`, using the configured environment secret. Apply an appropriate timestamp tolerance and persist deduplication by event ID. Retries keep the same event ID and exact body, with a fresh timestamp/signature. HTTP 2xx records receiver acceptance; acknowledgment is a separate operator action. A lost response can cause a retry after the receiver already accepted the event, so delivery is at least once.

408, 425, 429, 5xx and network/timeout failures retry with bounded exponential delay and bounded `Retry-After`. Other HTTP statuses exhaust the attempt budget; redirects are not followed. Up to four notifications run concurrently after a sweep. Retries occur on an eligible later sweep, so poll cadence can make delivery later than its minimum retry delay. Responses are bounded to 64 KiB and each request has an absolute timeout. After a crash, an in-flight attempt waits out its recorded deadline, retains the unknown-outcome reason and reuses its identity.

Each event pins its original complete source-config digest, exact notification-config digest, environment-reference names, destination ID and resolved canonical endpoint digest. Source labels, poll cadence and merchant policy changes do not move an event to a different receiver. Automatic acknowledgment, retirement and recovery transitions retain the incident's selected destination scope. Changing the notification configuration or the URL behind its environment reference pauses older events. Restoring the same original destination permits an explicit retry. To select the current configured destination for an existing incident, use a new explicit `notify` operation:

```bash
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" notify --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents \
  --incident ACTUAL_INCIDENT_UUID --revision ACTUAL_CURRENT_REVISION
```

This creates a new reminder event and selects that exact notification scope for the incident's future transitions. It does not rewrite the destination of an older pending event. The command process must have the intended environment values; a missing destination cannot be silently filled later. Signing-key rotation under the same environment reference and destination is supported.

To retry a paused or exhausted event at its same destination, read its actual attempt count and use:

```bash
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" retry --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents \
  --event ACTUAL_EVENT_UUID --attempts ACTUAL_ATTEMPTS --by 'Merchant operator'
```

A manual retry grants another bounded attempt budget without resetting the total attempt count, event ID or payload. An event already in flight cannot be retried or canceled. Use `cancel` with the same arguments to retire an unwanted pending/paused/exhausted notification, such as an old destination's event after selecting the replacement. An accepted notification is immutable; a deliberate additional message uses `notify`.

## Original support case handoff

The watcher retains an original SF93 four-file packet at a configured cadence and on incident open/recovery. For a complete outage, the baseline is the most recent retained successful capture, with its original timestamp; it is not an invented capture of the unavailable process. Recovery is a fresh original packet. If the watcher had never observed a usable process before the outage, the recovered incident can have only its actual follow-up capture.

Export against an existing private SF74 `.merchant-workspace.json` file and explicitly select one of the captured original route IDs whose method matches that workspace:

```bash
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" export --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents \
  --incident ACTUAL_INCIDENT_UUID --revision ACTUAL_CURRENT_REVISION \
  --workspace /srv/stellar/operator/merchant.merchant-workspace.json \
  --route dataset --out /srv/stellar/operator/incident-handoff-01
```

The new private directory contains `support-handoff.json`, `support.html`, `runtime-support.json`, the selected `incident.json`, and exact original `before/` and/or `after/` packet files. The existing original SF74 intake validates all packet hashes and scope. Distinct native sessions remain `SEPARATE_SESSIONS`; the handoff does not subtract them or manufacture a combined interval. Incident ID, registration, acknowledgment and dates travel through existing case metadata/notes, preserving the original handoff format.

In the existing SF74 Runtime stage, expand **Open a complete support handoff**, choose `support-handoff.json`, then **Open handoff as new case**. Use the existing **Save case** action to retain it in that application's case directory. No new incident dashboard or second case store is needed.

## Configuration, retention and backup

```bash
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" configure --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents \
  --config /srv/stellar/operator/watch.json --config-revision ACTUAL_CONFIG_REVISION
node "$SF93/incident-cli.mjs" prune --state /srv/stellar/operator/incidents
```

Configuration changes publish atomically. Results already being collected against an older configuration are discarded. Changes to a merchant's source ports or condition policy retire that registration's active incidents with `CONFIGURATION_CHANGED`, keeping their original captures. Retirement is not measured recovery. Same-source label/capture-cadence changes preserve active incident ownership. An unchanged notification registration can receive the retirement event at the same incident-selected endpoint.

Completed incidents follow the configured day/count retention; active incidents and incidents referenced by unfinished notifications are retained. Terminal notifications have their own retained-count limit. The unfinished queue is capped at 1,024 events. If full, incident work still records its state and exposes `notificationIssue: QUEUE_CAPACITY` plus the cumulative capacity counter; cancel obsolete events or let delivery finish, then explicitly notify the incident. Paused events already occupy a slot, so retrying one does not reserve a second slot.

Capture storage has a configured byte cap, 128 MiB by default. Referenced baseline, follow-up and latest merchant packets are preserved. Unreferenced packets and abandoned writes are collected under the same transaction lease. If a new packet cannot fit, the merchant reports `captureState: STORAGE_LIMIT`; the incident and its metadata still record the failure/recovery, and the missing packet is explicit. Increase the cap or reduce completed-case retention before collecting more evidence. Neither packet bytes nor state are silently truncated.

The private store exclusively owns `state.json`, reserved `state-UUID.tmp` files, its lock subdirectories and the `captures/` namespace (`capture-HASH.json`, `stage-capture-UUID.tmp`). Keep unrelated files elsewhere. Captures and state publish through file fsync, atomic rename and directory fsync; committed references publish before old captures are collected. Referenced capture reads verify content hashes and exact packet encoding. Export reads hold the same transaction lease so collection cannot remove their source mid-read.

For a consistent backup, stop this watcher and pause its operator commands, copy its entire private directory, and preserve file permissions. Reopen the same copied configuration with its original environment references and runtime endpoints. Pending notifications retain their original destination identity. State and exported support files are private merchant operational records.

# Saved Object buyers in the original incident and Support workspace

This extension connects a saved SF88 ObjectSession to the existing SF93 watcher and SF74 merchant case workspace. The operator reviews the original session identity, starts the existing watcher, acknowledges an incident, and opens the complete retained observation in the same Support case. Complete case export and reopen preserve the original native request views and byte checks.

The watcher only reads the saved buyer. It never purchases a chunk, starts an acquisition, assembles an output, finalizes a reservation, releases a payment or changes the buyer's ledger. Existing SF93 notification configuration and delivery controls continue to apply.

## Review the original session

Use the installed edition containing this extension, or run its original incident CLI from the checkout:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/incident-cli.mjs review-object \
  --session /absolute/private/original-object-session \
  --max-bytes 1073741824 --max-chunks 1000 --timeout-ms 30000 \
  --financial-after-seconds 300 --output-after-seconds 300
```

The result contains `object`, the exact normalized selection for an SF93 merchant registration, plus the inspected output, original terms, source URL and process observation. Review the original session ID, source intent, configuration SHA-256 and exact `session.json` SHA-256. An ordinary continued acquisition keeps that session binding; selecting a different buyer requires a new explicit configuration review.

The limits are receiving choices. `maxBytes` bounds the complete object size before chunk verification; `maxChunks` bounds the original request count; `timeoutMs` bounds the observation lifetime. The inspector hashes actual saved bytes using its original bounded buffer and checks cancellation between reads. Limits do not lower payment authorization or modify the original buyer. An observation that cannot cover the selected workload remains incomplete.

Each source is one original registration:

```js
const merchant = {
  id: "customer-object",
  label: "Customer data delivery",
  object: reviewedResult.object
};
```

Insert that full returned `object` into the existing private `stellar-forge.seller-watch-config.v1` document. Keep other merchant registrations and notification settings. An Object source cannot also contain seller/ops/delivery endpoint fields. The original watcher supports one to eight sources, including a mix of Object and existing seller sources.

For a new watcher, initialize its original store with that complete configuration. For an existing watcher, use its observed configuration revision:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/incident-cli.mjs init \
  --state /absolute/private/incident-store --config /absolute/private/watcher.json

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/incident-cli.mjs configure \
  --state /absolute/private/incident-store --config /absolute/private/watcher.json \
  --config-revision 1
```

The first command is for a new store; the second is for an existing one. Use the actual current revision, not an assumed value. The existing configuration transaction preserves incidents, retires bindings changed by the review and retains already-queued notification destinations.

## What an observation establishes

One observation contains a complete native accounting view before verification, the original byte-verifying Object report, and a complete accounting view afterward. Every page and every original request entry is retained. Each before/after accounting page also binds the exact original session-file SHA-256, so a changed snapshot or saved selection cannot hide behind unchanged payment terms. Accounting changes across those reads produce `CHANGED_DURING_READ`; missing data, a deadline or a workload limit cannot be interpreted as a recovered payment or completed output.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Finalized requests | Current per-request native `FINALIZED` or `IDEMPOTENT_FINALIZED` view recorded by the original job. It is a request count, not a monetary sum or a new ledger query. |
| Unresolved views | Other current attempted-request outcomes, including `NOT_FINALIZED`. Earlier `lastFinalized` remains history and cannot clear the current condition. |
| Not attempted | Original `NOT_ATTEMPTED` outcome. No attempted payment is inferred. |
| No payment required | Original `NO_PAYMENT_REQUIRED` outcome. It remains distinct from finalized paid requests. |
| Verified complete output | The original report verified every saved chunk and the complete object digest under the exact original session, configuration, ranges, snapshot, evidence and terms. |
| Process observation | Original lock/process information at inspection. It is separate from payment and output state. |
| Assembly receipt | Original recorded assembly history. The external assembled file is not revalidated by this watcher. |

The native `actualAtomicUnits`, receipt, completion time, request SHA-256, view status and earlier finalization data remain available per request. Their complete values are preserved. The monitor does not guess a currency, sum heterogeneous amounts or turn maximum authorizations into charges.

A poll applies only an observation captured within 30 seconds of application time, at most five seconds ahead of that clock, and later than the previous accepted capture for the same session. A slow source in the same sweep can therefore make an earlier capture stale. That complete old packet remains available as evidence, but it cannot advance a healthy streak, replace the last successful native observation or clear an incident.

A successful observation of an incomplete Object is a complete observation with incomplete output. It is not a successful delivery. A complete Object read during a changing accounting view remains unconfirmed for monitoring recovery until a coherent observation is available.

## Incident conditions and timing

| Existing watcher condition | Opens when | Clears through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OBJECT_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` | The source cannot supply a complete bounded observation for the configured failure-poll count. | Complete coherent observations under the original binding for the configured recovery-poll count. |
| `OBJECT_IDENTITY_CHANGED` | One confirmed mismatch in the selected manifest/configuration/intent or native binding. | Complete coherent observations matching the same reviewed binding. |
| `OBJECT_OUTPUT_INTEGRITY` | One confirmed native digest, range, snapshot, evidence or terms integrity failure. | Complete coherent observations without that integrity contradiction. |
| `OBJECT_FINANCIAL_UNRESOLVED` | A current unresolved request is at least `financialAfterSeconds` old for the configured failure-poll count. | Current coherent request views no longer satisfy the condition. |
| `OBJECT_FINALIZED_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` | A currently finalized request is at least `outputAfterSeconds` old while the selected object's output remains incomplete, for the configured failure-poll count. | Coherent verified complete output, or a coherent current financial view that no longer satisfies the condition. |

Unknown or invalid original timestamps remain unknown. The capture time is not substituted as a payment attempt time. A known aged request can open a condition even when another request's timestamp is unavailable; the unknown request cannot establish that all requests are below threshold. Future timestamps beyond the read tolerance do not provide an invented age.

Confirmed identity/integrity contradictions open immediately; the configured recovery-poll count still protects closure. The existing SF93 incident revision, acknowledgment, retention, notification queue, retry and cancellation semantics apply. Notification bodies use the original condition counts and source labels; the complete private capture is kept in the original incident store.

## Continue the incident in a Support case

Open the incident, review its before/follow-up Object facts and acknowledge who is handling it. The case handoff uses the **captured source ID**, not a new request or a new purchase. The source is represented as its original GET acquisition and explicitly mapped to the current case inputs.

Choose **Prepare incident case**. The existing server rereads the immutable capture files and validates their complete contents before building the original merchant support handoff. Review and download that handoff, then choose **Open prepared case** and save the case. The original source remains in the case rather than being replaced by a screenshot or a summary.

The Runtime support section also accepts the three original Object observation files directly:

- `object-observation.json`: reviewed selection, observation window, complete source hashes and recomputable summary.
- `object-report.json`: full original native Object report, or an explicit unavailable report.
- `object-accounting.json`: full before/after paginated native views, including unresolved current outcomes and earlier history.

Select **Saved Object buyer observation**, inspect all three files together and attach them to the chosen case position. Each file is bounded at 2 MB. A source too large for that format produces an explicit incomplete observation; it is never silently truncated into a successful capture.

The case presents current financial outcomes, verified output, process information, age thresholds, all original request entries, exact source identities and the native terms. A different case network/recipient or saved case scope remains visible as a mapping issue. A before/after comparison requires the same full reviewed Object selection and chronological observations. It does not subtract financial totals or claim a particular operator action caused recovery.

Use the existing complete Support handoff and saved-case exports. Fresh receiving can validate and review the three captured files without opening the old buyer path. Those paths are historical source lineage in the portable case. Live watching after relocation requires separately registering the actual original saved session at its supported location.

## Native API join

All console routes retain the original loopback/session-origin restrictions. The only new route is:

```
POST /api/incidents/:sourceId/inspect-object
```

Input is `{objectSourceId, expectedConfigRevision, maxBytes?, maxChunks?, timeoutMs?, financialAfterSeconds?, outputAfterSeconds?}`. It returns the exact original read-only review plus source ID and configuration revision. It neither writes the registration nor starts a watcher.

The existing configure/start/stop/ack/notify/case routes remain authoritative. The runtime inspect/review/export/import routes recognize `OBJECT_SESSION` through the three complete files, without adding a second case store or financial engine.

Source interfaces:

- `object-session.mjs: inspectObjectSession(directory, {signal?, maxBytes?, maxChunks?})` retains its original default behavior and adds bounded/cancellable read options, exact session-file SHA-256 and original attempt timestamps. The original read-only accounting pages also retain that session-file SHA-256.
- `object-source.mjs: reviewObjectSource(input, {signal?})` provides the explicit receiving review.
- `object-source.mjs: collectObjectObservation(merchant, signal)` supplies the existing SF93 sweep.
- `object-observation.mjs` validates and recomputes complete file observations and condition inputs.
- `object-runtime.mjs` renders those existing captures in SF74; it opens no source path and invokes no buyer.

This is source implementation and operating guidance. A particular customer, installed release or notification is complete only when its original native receiving result establishes that outcome.
